drivingQuestion: From what source does each tanna of the mishna derive his ruling about a fetus that died inside its mother's womb?
outcomeNote: Both tannaitic positions end with a source: the first tanna's from Rav Ḥisda's a fortiori plus the juxtaposition of Leviticus 11:39, and R' Yosei HaGelili's from Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak's reading of Leviticus 5:2 after R' Yitzḥak's reading is battered by Rav Aḥadvoi bar Ami; for the Rabbis that verse is given over entirely to Rabbi's verbal analogy.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי טַעְמָא דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא? אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: קַל וָחוֹמֶר, אִם הוֹעִילָה אִמּוֹ לְהַתִּירוֹ בַּאֲכִילָה, לֹא תּוֹעִיל לוֹ לְטַהוֹרֵיהּ מִידֵי נְבֵלָה?
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The Gemara asks: «What is the reason» for the ruling «of the first tanna? Rav Ḥisda said:» It is apparent through «an a fortiori» inference: «If» being inside «its mother is effective to permit it for consumption» through the slaughter of its mother even if the fetus was found dead inside the womb, then «should» being inside its mother «not» also «be effective to render it pure from» the impurity of «an animal carcass?»

segments.he: אַשְׁכְּחַן בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה, בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה מְנָלַן? אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְכִי יָמוּת מִן הַבְּהֵמָה״ – זוֹ בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה, ״אֲשֶׁר הִיא לָכֶם לְאׇכְלָה״ – זוֹ בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה, אִיתַּקַּשׁ בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה לִבְהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה: מָה בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה – עוּבָּרָהּ טָהוֹר, אַף בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה – עוּבָּרָהּ טָהוֹר.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «We found» a rationale for this halakha with regard to «a kosher animal; from where do we» derive that the same applies to «a non-kosher animal?» The Gemara answers that «the verse states:» “And when a domesticated animal dies, of those that you eat, one who touches its carcass shall be impure until the evening” (Leviticus 11:39). The Gemara interprets the verse as follows: «“And when a domesticated animal dies,” this» is referring to «a non-kosher animal; “of those that you eat,” this» is referring to «a kosher animal.» The verse thereby «juxtaposes a non-kosher animal to a kosher animal» with regard to imparting impurity of a carcass, and teaches that «just as» with regard to «a kosher animal, its fetus» that died in its womb is «pure,» as derived above through an a fortiori inference, «so too,» with regard to «a non-kosher animal, its» dead «fetus» is «pure.»

segments.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״וְכׇל הוֹלֵךְ עַל כַּפָּיו בְּכׇל הַחַיָּה הַהֹלֶכֶת וְגוֹ׳״ – מְהַלְּכֵי כַּפַּיִם בְּחַיָּה טִמֵּאתִי לָךְ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And» as for «Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, what is the reason» for his ruling? «Rabbi Yitzḥak said that the verse states» with regard to non-kosher animals that do not have cloven hooves: «“And whatever walks on its paws, among any [bekhol] undomesticated animal [ḥayya] that walks» on all fours, they are impure for you; whoever touches their carcass shall be impure until the evening” (Leviticus 11:27). Rabbi Yosei HaGelili expounds this verse as follows: Those animals «that walk on» their «paws,» i.e., that do not have cloven hooves, which are «inside» the body of «an animal, I rendered impure for you.» Rabbi Yitzḥak interprets the term bekhol as meaning: Inside the body of, and the word ḥayya as meaning: A live animal. Accordingly, he understands the verse to be referring to a dead fetus found inside a living animal.

segments.he: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, קָלוּט בִּמְעֵי פָרָה לִיטַמֵּא, דִּמְהַלְּכֵי כַפַּיִם בְּחַיָּה הוּא? מְהַלְּכֵי כַפַּיִם בִּמְהַלְּכֵי אַרְבַּע, וְהַאי מְהַלְּכֵי אַרְבַּע בִּמְהַלְּכֵי שְׁמֹנֶה הוּא.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «If that is so,» then a dead fetus with «non-cloven» hooves found «inside a cow should be impure,» despite the fact that it is from a kosher species, «as it is» an animal that «walks on» its «paws» that is «inside» the body of a kosher «animal.» The Gemara explains: The verse renders impure an animal that «walks upon» its four «paws» that is «inside» an animal «that walks» on «four» paws. «But this is» a case of an animal that «walks» on «four inside» an animal that «walks on eight.» Since the mother cow’s hooves are entirely split into two parts, it actually walks on eight parts and is not the animal referred to by the verse.

segments.he: פָּרָה בִּמְעֵי גָמָל לֹא תְּטַמֵּא, דִּמְהַלְּכֵי שְׁמֹנֶה בִּמְהַלְּכֵי אַרְבַּע הוּא, ״הוֹלֵךְ״, ״וְכׇל הוֹלֵךְ״ – לְרַבּוֹת פָּרָה בִּמְעֵי גָמָל.
segments.en: The Gemara raises another objection: If that is so, then a dead fetus in the form of «a cow,» which has eight parts to its legs, «inside the womb of a camel,» a non-kosher animal with non-cloven hooves, «should not be impure, as it is» an animal that «walks on eight inside» an animal that «walks on four,» and the verse is not referring to it. The Gemara responds that the verse could have stated: «Walks upon,» but instead states: «“And whatever walks upon,”» i.e., the addition of the word “whatever” serves «to include» a dead «cow» fetus «in the womb of a camel,» teaching that it is impure.

segments.he: קָלוּט בִּמְעֵי קְלוּטָה לִיטַמֵּא, דִּמְהַלְּכֵי אַרְבַּע בִּמְהַלְּכֵי אַרְבַּע הוּא! לְהָכִי אַהֲנִי קַל וָחוֹמֶר דְּרַב חִסְדָּא.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: If that is so, then a dead fetus with «non-cloven» hooves «inside the womb of» a cow with «non-cloven» hooves should «be impure, as it is» an animal that «walks on four inside» an animal that «walks on four,» but the halakha is that since the mother is a kosher species, it is pure. The Gemara explains: It is «to that» end that the «a fortiori» inference of «Rav Ḥisda is effective,» as it renders pure the fetuses of all kosher animals, even if their hooves are not fully cloven.

segments.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי: חֲזִיר בִּמְעֵי חֲזִירְתָּא לָא לִיטַמֵּא, דִּמְהַלְּכֵי שְׁמֹנֶה בִּמְהַלְּכֵי שְׁמֹנֶה הוּא!
segments.en: «Rav Aḥadvoi bar Ami objects to this» explanation that the verse renders impure only animals that walk on four inside animals that walk on four: If that is so, a dead «pig» fetus «inside the womb of a female pig should not be impure, as» a pig has cloven hooves, and so «it is» an animal that «walks on eight inside» an animal that «walks on eight,» and so the verse is not referring to it.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, מֵהָכָא: ״נֶפֶשׁ כִּי תִגַּע בְּכׇל טָמֵא אוֹ בְנִבְלַת חַיָּה טְמֵאָה אוֹ בְּנִבְלַת בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה אוֹ בְּנִבְלַת שֶׁרֶץ טָמֵא״.
segments.en: «Rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said» that Rabbi Yosei HaGelili’s opinion is derived «from here:» The verse states with regard to the sliding-scale offering brought by one who was unaware that he was impure when he ate consecrated food or entered the Temple: «“A person who touched anything impure, or the carcass of a non-kosher undomesticated animal, or the carcass of a non-kosher domesticated animal, or the carcass of an impure creeping animal,» and is guilty, it having being hidden from him that he is impure” (Leviticus 5:2).

segments.he: וְכִי נִבְלַת בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה מְטַמְּאָה, וּבִטְהוֹרָה לֹא מְטַמְּאָה? אֶלָּא אֵיזֶה זֶה? זֶה עוּבָּר, שֶׁבִּטְמֵאָה טָמֵא, וּבִטְהוֹרָה טָהוֹר.
segments.en: The verse presents a difficulty: «Does» only «a carcass of a non-kosher animal impart impurity, and» that «of a kosher» animal «not impart impurity?» The halakha is that both do. «Rather, what is this» animal to which the verse is referring? «This is a fetus, which» if «inside a non-kosher» animal is «impure, and» if «inside a kosher» animal is «pure.»

segments.he: וּמֵאַחַר דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִדְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק לְמָה לִי? אִי לָאו דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: כּוּלֵּיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי הוּא דַּאֲתָא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And since» this halakha «is derived from» the statement of «Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak, why do I» need the proof «of Rabbi Yitzḥak» from the verse: “And whatever walks on its paws, among any undomesticated animal that walks on all fours” (Leviticus 11:27)? The Gemara explains: «Were it not» for the derivation of «Rabbi Yitzḥak, I would say» that «the entire» verse expounded by Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak «comes to» teach only «that which Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi derived from it, as cited by the Gemara later on. Rabbi Yitzḥak’s statement «teaches us» that the verse is also to be expounded as Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak explained.

segments.he: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: נַמְתִּי לוֹ לְבֶן עַזַּאי, לָמַדְנוּ נִבְלַת בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה שֶׁמְּטַמְּאָה, וְנִבְלַת בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה שֶׁמְּטַמְּאָה, נִבְלַת חַיָּה טְמֵאָה שֶׁמְּטַמְּאָה.
segments.en: § It «is taught» in a baraita that «Rabbi Yonatan,» a student of Rabbi Yishmael, «says: I said [namti] to ben Azzai: We learned that a carcass of a kosher domesticated animal imparts impurity» from the verse: “And when a domesticated animal dies, of those that you eat, one who touches its carcass shall be impure until the evening” (Leviticus 11:39). «And» we learned that «a carcass of a non-kosher domesticated animal imparts impurity,» and «that a carcass of a non-kosher undomesticated animal imparts impurity,» from the verse: “A person who touched anything impure, or the carcass of a non-kosher undomesticated animal, or the carcass of a non-kosher domesticated animal” (Leviticus 5:2).

segments.he: נִבְלַת חַיָּה טְהוֹרָה לֹא לָמַדְנוּ מִנַּיִן? נָם לִי: ״כָּל הוֹלֵךְ עַל כַּפָּיו בְּכׇל הַחַיָּה הַהֹלֶכֶת״.
segments.en: But «we did not» yet «learn» about «a carcass of a kosher undomesticated animal. From where» is it derived that it imparts impurity? Ben Azzai «said to me» that this is derived from the verse: “And «whatever walks on its paws, among any undomesticated animal that walks» on all fours” (Leviticus 11:27). The inclusive term “among any” serves to include even a carcass of a kosher undomesticated animal among those that impart impurity.

segments.he: נַמְתִּי לוֹ: וְכִי נֶאֱמַר ״וְכׇל חַיָּה״? וַהֲלֹא לֹא נֶאֱמַר אֶלָּא ״בְּכׇל הַחַיָּה״, לִמְהַלְּכֵי כַּפַּיִם בְּחַיָּה הוּא דַּאֲתָא. נָם לִי: וּמָה יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר בְּדָבָר הַזֶּה?
segments.en: Rabbi Yonatan continues. «I said to» ben Azzai: «But does it state: And any undomesticated animal? Isn’t it stated only: “Among any undomesticated animal”?» And as explained earlier, this «comes to» teach «that» a dead fetus in the form of any of the animals that «walk on» their «paws inside an undomesticated animal imparts impurity. He said to me: And what does» Rabbi «Yishmael,» your teacher, «say about this matter?»

segments.he: נַמְתִּי לוֹ: ״וְכִי יָמוּת מִן הַבְּהֵמָה״ – זוֹ בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה, ״אֲשֶׁר הִיא לָכֶם לְאׇכְלָה״ – זוֹ בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה, לָמַדְנוּ חַיָּה בִּכְלַל בְּהֵמָה, וּבְהֵמָה בִּכְלַל חַיָּה.
segments.en: «I said to him» that Rabbi Yishmael derives all these halakhot from the verse: “And when a domesticated animal dies, of those that you eat, one who touches its carcass shall be impure until the evening” (Leviticus 11:39), as follows: «“And when a domesticated animal [habehema] dies,” this» is referring to «a non-kosher animal; “of those that you eat,” this» is referring to «a kosher animal.» And «we learned» that «a ḥayya is included» in the category of «a behema,» i.e., the term behema can also refer collectively to both domesticated and undomesticated animals. «And» likewise, «a behema is included» in the category of «a ḥayya.»

segments.he: חַיָּה טְהוֹרָה בִּכְלַל בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה, חַיָּה טְמֵאָה בִּכְלַל בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה,
segments.en: Furthermore, «a kosher ḥayya is included» when the Torah makes reference to «a kosher behema,» and «a non-kosher ḥayya is included» when the Torah makes reference to «a non-kosher behema.»

segments.he: בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה בִּכְלַל חַיָּה טְמֵאָה, בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה בִּכְלַל חַיָּה טְהוֹרָה, וּבַלָּשׁוֹן הַזֶּה אָמַר לִי: חֲבָל עַל בֶּן עַזַּאי שֶׁלֹּא שִׁימֵּשׁ אֶת רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
segments.en: And likewise, «a non-kosher behema is included» in the category of «a non-kosher ḥayya,» and «a kosher behema is included» in the category of «a kosher ḥayya.» Accordingly, although the verse here is referring to a behema, it is understood to be referring collectively to both a behema and a ḥayya, and teaches that the carcasses of both types impart impurity. «And» upon hearing this, ben Azzai «said to me in these words: Woe [ḥaval] unto ben Azzai, who did not serve Rabbi Yishmael.»

segments.he: חַיָּה בִּכְלַל בְּהֵמָה מְנָלַן? דִּכְתִיב: ״זֹאת הַבְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכֵלוּ שׁוֹר שֵׂה כְשָׂבִים וְגוֹ׳ אַיָּל וּצְבִי וְיַחְמוּר וְגוֹ׳״, הָא כֵּיצַד? חַיָּה בִּכְלַל בְּהֵמָה.
segments.en: The Gemara analyzes Rabbi Yishmael’s statement: «From where do we» derive that according to the Torah, «a ḥayya is included» in the category of «a behema? As it is written: “These are the behema that you may eat: An ox, a sheep,» and a goat, «a deer, and a gazelle, and a fallow deer,» and a wild goat, and an oryx, and an aurochs, and a wild sheep” (Deuteronomy 14:4–5). Despite employing the term “behema,” the verse also lists the deer and the gazelle, which are undomesticated animals. «How» is «this» possible? From here it is evident that «a ḥayya is included» by the Torah in the category of «a behema.»

segments.he: בְּהֵמָה בִּכְלַל חַיָּה מְנָלַן? דִּכְתִיב: ״זֹאת הַחַיָּה אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכְלוּ מִכׇּל הַבְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר עַל הָאָרֶץ כֹּל מַפְרֶסֶת פַּרְסָה״, הָא כֵּיצַד? בְּהֵמָה בִּכְלַל חַיָּה.
segments.en: «From where do we» derive that according to the Torah, «a behema is included» in the category of «a ḥayya? As it is written: “These are the ḥayya that you may eat, among all the behema that are on the earth. Whatever parts the hoof”» (Leviticus 11:2–3). «How» is «this» possible, that the verse mentions a ḥayya and then refers to a behema? This indicates that «a domesticated animal is included» in the category of «a ḥayya» by the Torah.

segments.he: חַיָּה טְהוֹרָה בִּכְלַל בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה – לְסִימָנִים.
segments.en: The Gemara further clarifies: The principle that «a kosher ḥayya is included» by the Torah in the category of «a kosher behema» is relevant «with regard to» the «distinguishing characteristics» of kosher animals. The Torah states with regard to a domesticated animal that only a species that chews its cud and has cloven hooves is kosher. Nevertheless, this requirement is understood as a reference to both domesticated and undomesticated animals.

segments.he: חַיָּה טְמֵאָה בִּכְלַל בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה – לְהַרְבָּעָה.
segments.en: The principle that «a non-kosher ḥayya is included» by the Torah in the category of «a non-kosher behema» is relevant «with regard to» the prohibition against «mating» one species with another. The Torah states the prohibition with regard to a behema: “You shall not let your animal [behema] mate with a diverse kind” (Leviticus 19:19). Nevertheless, this is understood as referring to both a behema and a ḥayya.

segments.he: בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה בִּכְלַל חַיָּה טְמֵאָה – לְכִדְרַבִּי.
segments.en: The principle that «a non-kosher behema is included» by the Torah in the category of «a non-kosher ḥayya» is relevant «with regard to that which Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi taught, «as it is taught» in a baraita: The verse delineates a case in which one is obligated to bring a sliding-scale offering as an atonement: “A person who touched anything impure, or the carcass of a non-kosher undomesticated animal [ḥayya], or the carcass of a non-kosher domesticated animal [behema], or the carcass of an impure creeping animal, and is guilty, it having being hidden from him that he is impure” (Leviticus 5:2). But the nature of the transgression for which the person requires atonement is not apparent from the verse.

segments.he: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֶקְרָא אֲנִי ״חַיָּה״, בְּהֵמָה לָמָּה נֶאֶמְרָה?
segments.en: «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «says:» Since a domesticated animal is also referred to as a ḥayya, it would be sufficient if «I would read,» i.e., the verse would write, only the clause about «a ḥayya,» and I would have known that one who touches a carcass of any non-kosher animal is impure. «Why,» then, «is» an explicit clause about «a behema stated?» It serves as the basis for a verbal analogy.

segments.he: נֶאֶמְרָה כָּאן ״בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה״, מָה לְהַלָּן טוּמְאַת קֹדֶשׁ – אַף כָּאן טוּמְאַת קֹדֶשׁ.
segments.en: «It is stated here,» with regard to one who is unaware that he touched an impure item: «“Non-kosher behema,” and it is» likewise «stated below,» with regard to one who was aware that he touched an impure item: «“Non-kosher behema,”» in the following verse: “And when any one shall touch any impure thing, whether it is the impurity of man, or a non-kosher behema, and then eats of the flesh of a peace offering to the Lord, that soul shall be cut off from its people” (Leviticus 7:21). «Just as below,» the verse is referring to the «defiling of sacrificial» foods, «so too here,» the reference is to the «defiling of sacrificial» foods, and therefore one must bring a sliding-scale offering as an atonement.

segments.he: בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה בִּכְלַל חַיָּה טְהוֹרָה, לִיצִירָה, דִּתְנַן: הַמַּפֶּלֶת מִין בְּהֵמָה חַיָּה וָעוֹף, בֵּין טְמֵאִין בֵּין טְהוֹרִין, אִם זָכָר – תֵּשֵׁב לְזָכָר.
segments.en: The Gemara clarifies the final statement: The principle that «a kosher behema is included» by the Torah in the category of «a kosher ḥayya» is relevant «with regard to» the «formation» of children. «As we learned» in a mishna (Nidda 21a): With regard to a woman «who miscarries» a fetus that appears to be in the form of «a type of behema, ḥayya, or bird, whether» it had the form of «a non-kosher» species «or a kosher» species, «if» the fetus is «a male,» then «she observes» the periods of impurity and purity required «for» giving birth to «a male.»

segments.he: אִם נְקֵבָה – תֵּשֵׁב לִנְקֵבָה.
segments.en: The mishna continues: And «if» the fetus is «a female,» then «she observes» the periods required «for» giving birth to «a female.» After giving birth to a male, a woman is impure for seven days, during which it is prohibited for her to engage in intercourse. During the next thirty-three days she may immerse in a ritual bath at any time, after which she is permitted to engage in intercourse even should she then experience a discharge of uterine blood. Nevertheless, during the entire forty-day period she may not enter the Temple or be in contact with consecrated foods. After giving birth to a girl, the length of each of these periods is doubled to fourteen days and sixty-six days, respectively (see Leviticus 12:2–5).

segments.he: אֵינוֹ יָדוּעַ – תֵּשֵׁב לְזָכָר וְלִנְקֵבָה,
segments.en: If the sex of the fetus is «unknown, she observes» the strictures of a woman who gave birth both «to a male and to a female.» Accordingly, it is prohibited for her to engage in intercourse for the fourteen days after birth, after which she immerses in a ritual bath. After that she is permitted to engage in intercourse despite any discharge of uterine blood until the fortieth day after birth, i.e., for thirty-three days following the seven days she would have been prohibited from engaging in intercourse if the fetus was male. The prohibition against entering the Temple, however, continues until eighty days have passed from the birth.

segments.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
segments.en: This is «the statement of Rabbi Meir.» The Gemara elsewhere (Nidda 22b) explains that Rabbi Meir derives his opinion from the fact that the term “formation” is used to describe both the formation of man: “Then the Lord God formed man” (Genesis 2:7), and the formation of animals and birds: “The Lord God formed every animal [ḥayya] of the field, and every bird of the air” (Genesis 2:19). Furthermore, he holds that the term “ḥayya” is referring to both domesticated and undomesticated animals, and concludes that a woman observes these periods of purity and impurity if the fetus has the form of any of these types of animals.

segments.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִצּוּרַת אָדָם אֵינוֹ וָלָד.
segments.en: «And the Rabbis say: Any» fetus «that is not of human form is not» regarded as «an offspring» with regard to observance of these periods of purity and impurity, and she is permitted to engage in intercourse provided she does not experience a discharge of uterine blood.

segments.he: וּלְרַבָּנַן, הַאי קְרָא לְמָה לִי?
segments.en: § The Gemara returns to explaining the opinion of the Rabbis, cited in the mishna, who hold that a dead fetus found inside its mother’s womb does not impart impurity, irrespective of whether it is of a kosher or a non-kosher animal. Rabbi Yosei HaGelili disagrees and holds that a dead fetus inside a non-kosher animal imparts impurity. He derives this from the verse: “A person who touched anything impure, or the carcass of a non-kosher ḥayya, or the carcass of a non-kosher behema, or the carcass of an impure creeping animal, and is guilty” (Leviticus 5:2), which is referring only to non-kosher animals. The Gemara asks: «And according to the Rabbis, why do I» need «this verse?»

segments.he: כּוּלֵּיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי הוּא דַּאֲתָא.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «The entire» verse «comes to» teach «that which Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi taught in the baraita cited earlier, that the verse obligates one to bring a sliding-scale offering only in cases where one partook of consecrated foods or entered the Temple while in a state of impurity of which one was unaware.

moves.cueHe: מאי טעמא דתנא קמא
moves.summary: the Gemara opens by asking the reason for the mishna's first tanna, whose ruling stands in the previous unit
moves.about: why the first tanna holds that a fetus that died inside its mother's womb is pure

moves.cueHe: אמר רב חסדא: קל וחומר
moves.summary: Rav Ḥisda supplies an a fortiori: if the mother permits the fetus for eating, she surely purifies it from carcass impurity
moves.about: supplying the first tanna's rationale in answer to the anonymous question

moves.cueHe: אשכחן בהמה טהורה, בהמה טמאה מנלן
moves.summary: the a fortiori reaches only kosher animals; whence the non-kosher case?
moves.about: whence the same purity applies to a fetus in a non-kosher animal, which Rav Ḥisda's a fortiori cannot reach

moves.cueHe: אמר קרא
moves.summary: Leviticus 11:39 is split into a non-kosher and a kosher clause, juxtaposing the two so the fetus rule carries over
moves.about: the anonymous voice answers its own מנלן by deploying the juxtaposition it has just drawn

moves.cueHe: ורבי יוסי הגלילי, מאי טעמא
moves.summary: and the reason for R' Yosei HaGelili, who holds the fetus of a non-kosher animal impure
moves.about: why R' Yosei HaGelili holds a dead fetus inside a non-kosher animal is impure

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יצחק: דאמר קרא
moves.summary: R' Yitzḥak grounds him in Leviticus 11:27 read as: paw-walkers inside a living animal I rendered impure for you
moves.about: answering the anonymous question about R' Yosei HaGelili's rationale

moves.cueHe: אלא מעתה, קלוט במעי פרה ליטמא
moves.summary: on that reading a non-cloven-hoofed fetus inside a cow would be impure
moves.about: if paw-walkers inside a living animal are impure, a non-cloven-hoofed fetus inside a cow should be impure too, yet it is not

moves.cueHe: מהלכי כפים במהלכי ארבע
moves.summary: the verse means paw-walkers inside a four-walker, and a cow walks on eight
moves.about: narrowing the verse to paw-walkers inside a four-walker, which a cow (walking on eight) is not

moves.cueHe: פרה במעי גמל לא תטמא
moves.summary: then a cow fetus inside a camel would be pure, being an eight-walker inside a four-walker
moves.about: on that narrowing, a cow fetus inside a camel would be pure, since it is an eight-walker inside a four-walker

moves.cueHe: הולך, וכל הולך – לרבות
moves.summary: the extra וכל includes the cow fetus inside a camel
moves.about: answering the camel difficulty by the inclusive וכל

moves.cueHe: קלוט במעי קלוטה ליטמא
moves.summary: then a non-cloven-hoofed fetus inside a non-cloven-hoofed cow would be impure, contrary to the halakha
moves.about: on that narrowing, a non-cloven-hoofed fetus inside a non-cloven-hoofed cow would be impure, though the halakha holds it pure

moves.cueHe: להכי אהני קל וחומר דרב חסדא
moves.summary: that case is covered by Rav Ḥisda's a fortiori, which purifies every fetus of a kosher mother
moves.about: answering the non-cloven-hoofed case by assigning it to Rav Ḥisda's a fortiori rather than to the verse

moves.cueHe: מתקיף לה רב אחדבוי בר אמי
moves.summary: Rav Aḥadvoi bar Ami: on that reading a pig fetus inside a sow would be pure, both walking on eight
moves.about: on the paw-walker-in-a-four-walker reading, a pig fetus inside a sow would be pure, since both walk on eight

moves.cueHe: אלא אמר רב נחמן בר יצחק, מהכא
moves.summary: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak substitutes Leviticus 5:2 as R' Yosei HaGelili's source
moves.about: replacing the failed derivation with a different verse as R' Yosei HaGelili's source

moves.cueHe: וכי נבלת בהמה טמאה מטמאה
moves.summary: since a kosher carcass also defiles, the verse's contrast must concern a fetus: impure in a non-kosher mother, pure in a kosher one
moves.about: since a kosher carcass also defiles, the verse's non-kosher/kosher contrast must be about a fetus

moves.cueHe: ומאחר דנפקא ליה מדרב נחמן בר יצחק, דרבי יצחק למה לי
moves.summary: why is R' Yitzḥak's derivation still needed?
moves.about: why R' Yitzḥak's derivation is still needed once Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak's verse yields the same halakha

moves.cueHe: אי לאו דרבי יצחק, הוה אמינא
moves.summary: without it one would have given the whole verse over to Rabbi's derivation
moves.about: without R' Yitzḥak one would have assigned the whole verse to Rabbi's derivation alone

moves.cueHe: תניא, אמר רבי יונתן
moves.summary: the baraita in which R' Yitzḥak's derivation from בכל החיה is recorded, as a dialogue between R' Yonatan and ben Azzai
moves.about: bringing the baraita in which R' Yonatan's exchange with ben Azzai over the same verse is recorded

moves.cueHe: נמתי לו לבן עזאי, למדנו
moves.summary: R' Yonatan: we have sources for three carcass categories; whence a kosher undomesticated animal?
moves.about: whence a kosher undomesticated animal's carcass imparts impurity, once the other three cases are accounted for

moves.cueHe: נם לי: כל הולך על כפיו
moves.summary: ben Azzai answers from the inclusive בכל החיה of Leviticus 11:27
moves.about: answering that the inclusive בכל החיה covers a kosher undomesticated animal

moves.cueHe: נמתי לו: וכי נאמר וכל חיה
moves.summary: the verse says בכל החיה, not וכל חיה, so it teaches about paw-walkers inside an animal, not a kosher ḥayya's carcass
moves.about: the verse says בכל החיה, not וכל חיה, so it teaches about paw-walkers inside an animal and cannot include a kosher ḥayya's carcass

moves.cueHe: נם לי: ומה ישמעאל אומר בדבר הזה
moves.summary: ben Azzai asks what R' Yishmael, R' Yonatan's master, holds
moves.about: what R' Yishmael, R' Yonatan's teacher, holds about the source for a kosher undomesticated animal's carcass

moves.cueHe: נמתי לו: וכי ימות מן הבהמה
moves.summary: R' Yonatan reports R' Yishmael's derivation: behema and ḥayya each include the other, so the kosher ḥayya's carcass is covered
moves.about: answering ben Azzai's question about R' Yishmael's view

moves.cueHe: ובלשון הזה אמר לי: חבל על בן עזאי
moves.summary: ben Azzai concedes: woe to ben Azzai, who did not serve R' Yishmael
moves.about: conceding, on hearing R' Yishmael's derivation, that his own reading was inferior and that he never studied with R' Yishmael

moves.cueHe: חיה בכלל בהמה מנלן
moves.summary: the Gemara audits the baraita's premises: whence is a ḥayya included in behema?
moves.about: whence the baraita's claim that a ḥayya is included in the category of a behema

moves.cueHe: דכתיב: זאת הבהמה אשר תאכלו
moves.summary: Deuteronomy 14:4-5 lists deer and gazelle under the heading behema
moves.about: answering its own מנלן on ḥayya being included in behema

moves.cueHe: בהמה בכלל חיה מנלן
moves.summary: and whence is a behema included in ḥayya?
moves.about: whence the baraita's claim that a behema is included in the category of a ḥayya

moves.cueHe: דכתיב: זאת החיה אשר תאכלו
moves.summary: Leviticus 11:2-3 heads a behema list with the word ḥayya
moves.about: answering its own מנלן on behema being included in ḥayya

moves.cueHe: חיה טהורה בכלל בהמה טהורה – לסימנים
moves.summary: the baraita's kosher-ḥayya clause is stated for the kosher signs
moves.about: identifying which halakha the baraita's clause 'a kosher ḥayya is in the category of a kosher behema' is stated for — the kosher signs

moves.cueHe: חיה טמאה בכלל בהמה טמאה – להרבעה
moves.summary: the non-kosher-ḥayya clause is stated for the prohibition of crossbreeding
moves.about: identifying the clause 'a non-kosher ḥayya is in the category of a non-kosher behema' as stated for the prohibition of crossbreeding

moves.cueHe: בהמה טמאה בכלל חיה טמאה – לכדרבי
moves.summary: the non-kosher-behema clause is stated for Rabbi's verbal analogy
moves.about: identifying the clause 'a non-kosher behema is in the category of a non-kosher ḥayya' as stated for Rabbi's verbal analogy

moves.cueHe: דתניא, רבי אומר: אקרא אני חיה
moves.summary: Rabbi asks why the verse states behema at all, since behema is included in ḥayya
moves.about: why the verse states behema when behema is already included in ḥayya

moves.cueHe: נאמרה כאן בהמה טמאה, ונאמר להלן
moves.summary: a verbal analogy on בהמה טמאה fixes the sliding-scale offering as the case of defiling sacrificial food
moves.about: bringing the parallel בהמה טמאה verse as the second term of a verbal analogy

moves.cueHe: בהמה טהורה בכלל חיה טהורה, ליצירה
moves.summary: the kosher-behema clause is stated for the formation of a miscarried fetus
moves.about: identifying the clause 'a kosher behema is in the category of a kosher ḥayya' as stated for the formation of a miscarried fetus

moves.cueHe: דתנן: המפלת מין בהמה חיה ועוף
moves.summary: the mishna on a woman who miscarries an animal-form fetus, per R' Meir
moves.about: bringing the mishna on a woman who miscarries a fetus in animal form

moves.cueHe: וחכמים אומרים: כל שאינו מצורת אדם אינו ולד
moves.summary: the Rabbis dissent: only a human-form fetus counts as offspring
moves.about: whether a woman who miscarries a fetus in the form of an animal, ḥayya or bird observes the postpartum periods of impurity and purity, or whether only a human-form fetus counts as offspring

moves.cueHe: ולרבנן, האי קרא למה לי
moves.summary: what does Leviticus 5:2 teach for the Rabbis, who purify the fetus even in a non-kosher animal?
moves.about: what the sliding-scale offering verse teaches according to the Rabbis, who hold a dead fetus is pure even in a non-kosher animal

moves.cueHe: כוליה לכדרבי הוא דאתא
moves.summary: for them the whole verse is given over to Rabbi's verbal analogy
moves.about: for the Rabbis the whole verse is given over to Rabbi's verbal analogy about defiling sacrificial food
